audience.notes: Australian couple in their 30s, AUD 150K+, wedding week for 60 to 150 guests, drawn to a private villa for privacy and control. Fear A: the villa package looks complete but permits, power, toilets, guest beds, wet-weather cover and community fees sit outside it. Fear B: a private villa has no resort team, so nobody is accountable for suppliers, guests and the night itself. Paying parent: who holds which contract, itemised quotes, deposit terms. Anti-persona: the SERP is IDR price lists, 30-guest bundles and holiday deals; do not echo them.

payload.search_intent: Commercial investigation, mixed with villa-rental and holiday intent. The reader wants to know if a private villa suits their wedding and what a villa package really covers.
payload.angle: The villa-specific spoke: when a private villa beats a resort for a Bali wedding week, what exclusive use actually gives you, what a villa package covers and the long list it leaves to you (permits, banjar fees, curfew, generator, toilets, guest stays, wet-weather cover, access, neighbours), how villa capacity really works, who holds the vendor list, and the questions to put to the villa manager. Shows the invisible work a Wedded Advisor runs when there is no resort team behind you.

outline.h2: What Bali villa wedding packages include
outline.answers: Direct answer plus the categories a villa package is built around.
must_include: 'bali villa wedding packages' in the first 100 words and in this H2.

Direct answer in the first 60 words: a villa package usually bundles exclusive or event use of a private villa for a set time, its in-house staff, a set number of bedrooms for a set number of nights, and a planner's core set-up; what it covers varies by villa and must be read line by line.

Categories only (no provider list, no prices): event fee for the villa, villa staff (butlers, housekeeping, security), included bedrooms and nights, ceremony and reception set-up, basic styling, on-day coordination, sometimes catering through a preferred caterer.

One line linking up to the parent for the general package categories, conditional DRAFT link, descriptive anchor (e.g. 'our guide to what Bali packages cover in general'). Do not repeat the parent's three-type table.

outline.h2: Private villa or resort: which suits your wedding week
outline.answers: When a villa is the better choice and when a resort is. Uses secondary keyword 'bali villa wedding'.
must_include: Prose comparison, not a grid (the parent owns the comparison grid): privacy and exclusive use, freedom to bring suppliers, the whole group under one roof versus a resort's rooms, food and drink control; against that, no resort back-of-house, limited beds, more to arrange, house and community rules.
Define exclusive use: the whole property is yours for the agreed dates, closed to other guests. Ask whether the package is exclusive use or event use only.
Fair to both: a resort suits couples who want one team and one bill; a villa suits couples who want privacy and are prepared for more coordination.

Optional link: /destination-weddings/destination-wedding-venues (LIVE per Firecrawl, proposed for link-map) for the wider villa-versus-resort point; and the Lake Como exclusive-use villa article as a cross-destination example, only if added to link-map.

outline.h2: What a villa package usually leaves out
outline.answers: The main gap. The invisible work and costs. Addresses fear A.
must_include: Table or checklist framed as 'check whether yours includes': event permits and police or village notifications; banjar (local community) fees and who pays them; noise curfew and amplified music cut-off; generator hire and power load for lighting, sound and kitchen; portable or extra toilets for the guest count; guest accommodation beyond the villa's beds; wet-weather cover (marquee or covered space, hire and decision time); access for coaches, vendor trucks and guests (narrow lanes, steps, parking); neighbours and shared driveways; vendor meals; security and overtime; service charge and tax.

Each item is a planning check, not a figure. Banjar fee, generator and corkage: link the Bali cost guide with a descriptive anchor (e.g. 'our Bali wedding budget guide'), which lists them as hidden costs; no amounts.
Permit and curfew facts only from official or venue-published sources; otherwise write 'confirm with the villa manager and your planner'. Unsourced specifics become [[NEEDS: research answer]].
Link /destination-wedding-packages with a descriptive anchor (e.g. 'how our destination wedding packages are built').

outline.h2: How many guests a Bali villa can hold
outline.answers: Capacity explained: why the number on the package is not the whole answer.
must_include: Four numbers to ask for: standing event capacity, seated dinner capacity, beds (sleeping capacity), and parking or drop-off space.
For 60 to 150 guests, most of the group sleeps elsewhere: plan nearby villas or a hotel room block and transfers each night (link /travel, descriptive anchor).
Ceremony, dinner and dancing may need different spaces and a turnaround; ask who resets and how long it takes.
No capacity figures for named villas unless from our own venue profiles.

outline.answers: Preferred, mandatory and open supplier lists, and who contracts whom. Addresses fear B and the paying parent.
must_include: Three set-ups: villa with mandatory suppliers; villa with a preferred list and outside suppliers allowed for a fee; open villa where you or your planner contract everyone.
Who holds each contract, who carries insurance and who answers on the night if a supplier is late.
Outside supplier fees and corkage: ask; no figures.
Where a Wedded Advisor fits: one point of contact across villa, suppliers and guest logistics (wording from brand-profile only).

outline.h2: Questions to ask the villa manager
outline.answers: Villa-specific questions only; none of the parent's ten questions repeated.
must_include: 8 to 10 numbered questions, villa-specific, e.g. Is this exclusive use or event use, and from when to when? Which permits do you arrange and which do we? Are banjar fees included, and who deals with the banjar? What is the music curfew? What power is on site and is a generator needed? How many toilets, and do we need extra? Where do coaches and vendor trucks stop? Do neighbours share the access or the view? What is the wet-weather space and when is the call made? Which staff are on duty on the night and until when?

Cross-check against the parent's list before writing; drop any duplicate (parent covers exclusions, service and tax, rain decision, on-day contact, fixed suppliers, overtime and curfew in general, rooms and transfers, payment and cancellation, legal ceremony). Villa wording must be specific to the property.

outline.h2: The legal side and when bespoke planning fits
outline.answers: One legal paragraph linking up, then the bespoke case. Addresses fear B.
must_include: Legal: one paragraph only. A villa ceremony is usually symbolic; the two routes (marry in Australia then celebrate in Bali, or a legal Indonesian wedding) are covered in the parent and in /expert-advice/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married; recognition back home links /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate. Official source wording only (Smartraveller). No legal routes table.

Bespoke: signals that a villa wedding needs a planner (more than one event, a guest list above the villa's beds, imported suppliers, cultural ceremonies). What the Wonderland Concierge and a Wedded Advisor coordinate: villa shortlist and contract, permits and community liaison, supplier contracts, room blocks, transfers, wet-weather plan, run sheet. No guarantees. No prices.
Links: /destinations/asia/bali (descriptive anchor, e.g. 'our Bali destination guide'), /wonderland-concierge. Optional one-line real wedding from link-map's Bali rows. Soft CTA here.
